scripts.radio:
Welcome to Kenya on Record, keeping public interest on the ledger. 

First, public property belongs to the public. The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission has officially recovered a 2.7-acre school playground in Kikuyu following a landmark court ruling. For years, private interests have attempted to carve up recreational spaces meant for our children. This judgment sends a direct message to land cartels: title deeds acquired through fraud will remain worthless paper.

In the capital, taps ran dry as Nairobi Water shut down supply across several estates for three days of pipeline maintenance. While scheduled repairs are necessary to plug system losses, Nairobi City County must ensure rationing schedules are strictly adhered to and that water bowsers do not exploit desperate residents in the interim.

Meanwhile, human rights defenders under Linda Mwananchi have raised alarm following the reported abduction of Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya. The group is demanding an immediate investigation from Kenyan authorities, stressing that Kenya's territorial integrity must never be compromised to silence foreign dissidents seeking refuge.

Kwa ufupi wiki hii: Shirika la EACC limefaulu kurejesha ekari 2.7 za uwanja wa shule huko Kikuyu baada ya uamuzi wa mahakama. Nairobi Water ilisitisha usambazaji wa maji kwa siku tatu ili kufanya ukarabati wa mabomba, huku wanaharakati wa Linda Mwananchi wakilaani kutekwa nyara kwa mwanaharakati wa Tanzania, Twaha Mwaipaya, hapa nchini. Kaa macho, linda haki yako.
scripts.voice_note:
Hello everyone, Kenya on Record here with your weekly brief.

A big win for public assets: EACC has recovered a 2.7-acre school playground in Kikuyu through a court order. If you've been eying public school land, take note—the courts are revoking those illegal titles.

In Nairobi, Nairobi Water's three-day pipeline shutdown disrupted several estates. Upgrades are fair, but we demand predictability and an end to artificial cartels hiking water prices during maintenance.

Finally, human rights group Linda Mwananchi has called out the reported abduction of Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya in Kenya. Our sovereignty and constitutional guarantees on asylum cannot be discarded quietly.

Keep safe, question the paperwork, and look out for your community.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Public utilities and school grounds cannot be privatised legally. Always do an official search at Ardhisasa or Lands Registry before buying land.
scripts.reels: For years, private grabbers thought they could swallow a 2.7-acre school playground in Kikuyu. They were wrong. Following a decisive court ruling, the EACC has reclaimed the land for the community. The lesson is plain: public property cannot be laundered through corrupt paperwork. If you bought grabbed school land, you don't own property—you own a lawsuit waiting to happen.
